grammar_focus: 过去完成时(在另一过去动作之前发生·含被动 had been done)、had expected/meant/thought to do(过去想做/原以为而未成的事)、must have done(对过去的推测)、as if/as though + 过去完成(与过去相反的比拟)、be absorbed in/on one's own/not that…but that(NCE3 第三册 Unit 3 无 KS 页,考点由课文结构 + Notes on the text 自取;原创承载·返乡寻旧村发现故乡已沉入人造水库的怀旧故事·丧亲背景淡化为温和思乡·无暴力;美语化 odometer/gas/tire)
scene: 我停下车,让发动机冷却一下,同时看看地图。我本以为这时已接近目的地,可周围一切对我仍很陌生。我五岁那年父亲就带我出了国,那是十八年前的事了。他当年决定移居国外,是想为我们俩开创更好的生活;到了新的国度,他一心扑在工作和计划上。他总打算有朝一日回去,但只为探望,绝不久留——他和我一样,根早已深深扎在了新的土地里。可他仍渴望再见见家乡的老人,再走一走他出生的那个村子。我们原定一同回去,可动身前几个月他病倒了;当他知道自己去不成时,便要我答应独自走这一趟。我下飞机后第二天就租了一辆车,还买了一本详尽的地图册。它在跨越乡野的旅途上很管用,但我原以为最后一段路用不着它——倒不是我真记得什么,而是父亲曾一遍遍给我讲过,离最近的小镇之后,每一个路标处该看到些什么,因此我确信自己会认出那片熟悉的土地。唉,我错了,我现在迷路了。我看看地图,又看看里程表。离开小镇我已走了十英里,照父亲的说法,这时我眼前应是山谷里的农场和村舍,远处还有村里教堂的尖顶。可我看不见山谷,看不见农场村舍,也看不见尖顶——只有一片湖。我断定自己一定在什么地方拐错了弯,便掉头沿原路返回,一路频频看地图,结果又回到了同一个拐角。奇怪的是,那片湖在地图上根本没有标出。我觉得自己仿佛闯进了一个梦境之国,一切都不在它该在的地方。正当我坐着琢磨下一步怎么办,一个骑马的人出现在地平线上,朝我这边骑来。我等他走近,便问他去老家村子的路。他温和地告诉我:那个村子已经没有了。我以为他误解了我,又说了一遍村名。这一次,他只是指了指那片湖。他说,村子不复存在了,因为整个山谷都被淹没了;那片湖不是天然的,而是一座人工修建的水库——在它平静的水面之下某处,躺着父亲一辈子都念念不忘的家。

grammar_card.title: 过去完成时 / had expected to do / must have done / as if + 过去完成
grammar_card.intro: ①过去完成时(had + 过去分词)表在另一过去动作之前已完成,常用于叙事回溯:the village had disappeared before I came。②had expected/meant/thought/planned to do,表过去原打算/原以为而未实现的事:I had expected to be near my objective。③must + have + 过去分词,对过去作肯定推测:I must have taken a wrong turning。④as if/as though + 过去完成,表与过去相反的比拟:I felt as if I had stumbled into a dream。

rows: I had expected to be near
I must have taken a wrong turning
as if I had stumbled into a dream

specialRules.rule: 叙事已在过去,更早发生的事用过去完成时 had done;被动则 had been done(the valley had been submerged)。
as if/as though 后接过去完成,表示与过去事实相反的比拟,并非真的发生过。
美式用词:odometer(里程表,英式 milometer)、gas(汽油,英式 petrol)、tire(轮胎,英式 tyre)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What had happened to the narrator's old village?
options: It had been submerged under a reservoir
It had grown into a city

passage: I stopped to let the car cool off and to study the map. I had expected to be near my objective by now, but everything still seemed alien to me. I was only five when my father had taken me abroad, and that was eighteen years ago. He had decided to emigrate to build a better life for the two of us, and in the new land he became absorbed in his work and his plans. He always meant to go back one day, but only for a visit, never to stay — his roots and mine had become too firmly embedded in the new soil. Still, he longed to see the old folk again and to walk once more through the village where he was born. He fell ill a few months before we had planned to travel together, and when he knew he could not go, he made me promise to make the journey on my own. I hired a car the day after landing and bought a comprehensive book of maps, which I found most helpful on the cross-country journey, but which I had thought I would not need on the last stage. It was not that I actually remembered anything, but that my father had described, over and over, what I should see at every milestone after leaving the nearest town, so that I was positive I would recognize the place as familiar territory. Well, I had been wrong, for I was now lost. I looked at the map and then at the odometer. I had come ten miles since leaving the town, and at this point, according to my father, I should have been looking at farms and cottages in a valley, with the spire of the village church showing in the far distance. I could see no valley, no farms, no cottages and no spire — only a lake. I decided that I must have taken a wrong turning somewhere, so I drove back and began to retrace my route, taking frequent glances at the map. I landed up at the same corner. The strange thing was that the lake was not marked on the map at all. I felt as if I had stumbled into a dream country, where nothing was where it should be. As I sat wondering what to do, a man on horseback appeared on the horizon, riding in my direction. I waited until he came near and asked him the way to our old village. He told me, gently, that there was no longer any village. I thought he must have misunderstood me, so I repeated its name. This time he simply pointed to the lake. The village no longer existed, he said, because the whole valley had been submerged. The lake was not a natural one, but a man-made reservoir, and somewhere beneath its calm surface lay the home my father had never stopped dreaming of.

stage5.stem: "When I returned, the village ___ already disappeared under the lake."(过去完成时,填助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 我回来时,村子早已消失在湖底。

stage5.stem: "The valley ___ been submerged long before I came back."(过去完成时的被动:早已被淹,填助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 早在我回来前很久,山谷就已被淹没。

stage5.stem: "I was lost, though my father ___ described every milestone to me."(过去完成时,表更早发生)
stage5.stem_cn: 我迷了路,尽管父亲早把每个路标都对我描述过。

stage5.stem: "I ___ expected to be near my objective by now, but I was lost."(过去想做/原以为而未成:用过去完成时 + expect,填助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 我本以为这时已接近目的地,却迷了路。

stage5.stem: "I bought maps I ___ thought I would not need on the last stage."(过去完成时表“原以为”)
stage5.stem_cn: 我买了些原以为最后一段用不上的地图。

stage5.stem: "My father always ___ to go back one day, but only for a visit."(过去的打算“总打算做…”,填动词过去式)
stage5.stem_cn: 父亲总打算有朝一日回去,但只为探望。

stage5.stem: "I ___ have taken a wrong turning somewhere, for I was lost."(对过去的推测“一定…了”)
stage5.stem_cn: 我一定是在什么地方拐错了弯,所以迷了路。

stage5.stem: "The stranger ___ have misunderstood me, I thought, so I repeated the name."(对过去的推测,填表推测的词)
stage5.stem_cn: 我想这个陌生人一定误解了我,于是又说了一遍名字。

stage5.stem: "Someone ___ have built this reservoir while I was away."(must ___ 过去分词:对过去的推测,填这个助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 我离开期间一定有人建了这座水库。

stage5.stem: "I felt as if I ___ stumbled into a dream country."(as if + 过去完成,表与过去相反)
stage5.stem_cn: 我觉得自己仿佛闯进了一个梦境之国。

stage5.stem: "Everything looked as though it ___ been rearranged overnight."(as though + 过去完成)
stage5.stem_cn: 一切看起来仿佛一夜之间被重新摆放过。

stage5.stem: "He spoke as if he ___ known the valley all his life."(as if + 过去完成,表与过去相反)
stage5.stem_cn: 他说起话来,仿佛一辈子都熟悉那座山谷。

stage5.stem: "In the new land my father became ___ in his work and his plans."(be ___ in sth:全神贯注于,填过去分词)
stage5.stem_cn: 在新的国度,父亲一心扑在工作和计划上。

stage5.stem: "He asked me to make the journey on my ___."(on one's ___:独自、靠自己,填这个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 他让我独自完成这趟旅程。

stage5.stem: "It was not that I remembered the road, ___ that my father had described it."(not that… ___ that…:不是因为…而是因为,填中间的连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 并非我记得这条路,而是父亲曾描述过它。

stage5.stem: "Something foreign and unfamiliar feels ___."(“异国的、陌生的”用哪个词)
"A large man-made lake for storing water is a ___."(“水库”用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 人工修建、用于蓄水的大湖。

stage5.stem: "To go back over the same route is to ___ it."(“返回、重走”用哪个词)
